accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary Jordan pair V, determine the full normal subgroup structure of the projective elementary group PE(V); equivalently, classify all normal subgroups of PE(V).

evidence.quote: 3.1. The normal subgroup structure of PE(V ). The problem is quite easily stated: Given a Jordan pair V , describe all normal subgroups of PE(V ).

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the two theorems cited from [Lo5] continue to hold for broader classes of Jordan pairs: namely, whether PE(V) is perfect exactly when V has no simple factors isomorphic to (F2, F2), (F3, F3), or (H2(F2), H2(F2)), and whether PE(V) is simple exactly when V is simple and avoids those exceptional factors.
accepted.context_brief: Extend perfectness and simplicity criteria for PE(V)

evidence.quote: The problem is to find out if these two theorems of [Lo5] hold for more general Jordan pairs. It follows from (b) that is natural to assume simplicity of V for the second theorem.

accepted.question_text: Let I be an ideal of a Jordan pair V, let can: V -> V/I be the canonical map, and let PE(V, I) be the kernel of the induced surjective homomorphism PE(can): PE(V) -> PE(V/I). Describe the group PE(V, I) by explicit generators and relations.
accepted.context_brief: Generators and relations for relative group PE(V, I)

evidence.quote: Problem: describe PE(V, I) by generators and relations.

accepted.question_text: Assume V is defined over a field F and has a fully idempotent root grading R that is a division grading, meaning that every nonzero x in a root space V_alpha makes Q(x)|V_alpha invertible on the opposite root space. In the low-rank cases 2 <= rank R <= 4, is it true that whenever the Steinberg group St(V, R) is not centrally closed, every root space V_alpha must be one-dimensional over F and the field F must satisfy exactly the exceptional small-field restrictions listed in table (3.2.1)?

evidence.quote: Preliminary investigations lead us to conjecture: (C) If St(V, R) is not centrally closed then dimF V_alpha = 1 for all alpha in R1 and F satisfies the restrictions of table (3.2.1).

accepted.question_text: In the rank-one case, let J be a division Jordan algebra and let St(J) denote the rank-one Steinberg group defined in this section. Is St(J) centrally closed for every such J except the finite fields F_q with q in {2, 3, 4, 9}?

evidence.quote: This leads us to ask: (Q) Is St(J) centrally closed whenever J != Fq with q in {2, 3, 4, 9} ?

accepted.question_text: Let pi: St(V, R) -> PE(V) be the homomorphism from Theorem 2.11(a), and assume the root system R is irreducible of finite rank. Find sufficient conditions under which the kernel Ker(pi) is central.
accepted.context_brief: Centrality of the kernel of pi

evidence.quote: 3.3. Centrality of Ker(pi). Let pi : St(V, R) -> PE(V ) be the homomorphism of Theorem 2.11(a). ... The problem here is: find sufficient conditions for Ker(pi) to be central if R has finite rank.

accepted.question_text: For split root graded Jordan pairs V, can the basis-free presentation method pioneered by van der Kallen be generalized so that it treats the Steinberg group St(V, R) in a uniform, case-free way?

evidence.quote: Can the method of [vdK] be generalized to treat St(V, R), V split root graded, in a case-free manner?
